title: The outer focal-pedal area product in odd elliptic billiards

early_independence.prior_exposure: Earlier editorial work on row154/23334001 odd-period pedal-antipedal area product and row155/23394004 outer focal inversion product, plus learned elliptic/Poncelet background and other unrelated catalogue roles. Present manuscript embedded assertions necessarily read as author assertions.

whole_original_abstract_tex:
For a fixed odd-periodic billiard family between strictly nested confocal
ellipses, project each original focus onto the ordered side lines of the outer
tangent polygon. We prove that the product of the two signed pedal areas is
constant, for every coprime winding, including stars. This proves the
experimental assertion labelled $k_{605,a}$ in the 2020 arXiv invariant list
and $k_{606}$ in its published companion. The focal-foot map has paired
collinear residues; its cyclic area consequently has only two possible simple
poles on a reduced torus. Reflection and an imaginary antiperiod provide the
complementary zeros. The argument uses established elliptic-function methods.
We explain connections to generalized Landen identities and recent focal
inversion results; historical priority of this particular application remains
undetermined. Exact controls and separately labelled numerical diagnostics
accompany this unrefereed, extensively AI-assisted note.

full_native_Description: For a fixed odd least-period billiard family between strictly nested nondegenerate confocal ellipses, project the two original foci onto the ordered side lines of the outer tangent polygon. We prove that the product of the two signed pedal areas is constant for every admitted coprime winding, including stars. Fixed repeated traversals and the circular case are treated separately. This proves the experimental assertion k605,a in Reznik-Garcia-Koiller arXiv2004.12497v11, Table7, renamed k606 in the published companion; its earliest inspected source-series statement is v1,26April2020,Table5 k604. The complete proof uses the explicit focal-foot map, paired collinear residues, reduced real period and complementary zeros on a compact torus. Classical auxiliary-circle geometry, Stachel canonical coordinates, Jacobi and cyclic elliptic identities, older Poncelet-area methods and Khare-Sukhatme2004 generalized Landen identity are explicitly credited. The archive provides a complete alternative geometric reduction to that old identity and a pole-space comparison to Ferudun2026 original focal-inversion areas; those additional geometric applications are distinguished from literal earlier printed target proofs. Two independent bounded priority investigations verified no earlier printed general proof of this exact target in the inspected corpus; historical novelty and public priority remain undetermined. Source editions, actual read passages, hashes and access gaps are documented, including incomplete final-journal comparison and inaccessible related text. No first-proof, new general elliptic-method, absolute-priority or current-worldwide-open claim is made. The deposit includes the research note and a portable source/verification archive preserving the original submission, exact controls, separately labelled uncertified numerical diagnostics, authored audit records and reproducibility limitations. Finite checks support the universal proof. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, source investigation, writing, computation and independent internal adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification.
